title: Absorbance and concentration: the Beer–Lambert law
caption: A = εcl: for a fixed path length and wavelength, absorbance is proportional to concentration, so standards of known concentration give a straight calibration line from which an unknown can be read. At high concentrations the real curve flattens below the line, so samples must be diluted into the linear range. Idealised numbers.
alt: A dashed straight line of absorbance rising by 0.15 per concentration unit, and a solid curve that follows it at first and then flattens; an unknown absorbance of 0.6 is read off the straight line as a concentration of 4.
description: Absorbance is proportional to concentration over a working range: the straight line.
Standards of known concentration make the calibration curve.
An unknown with absorbance 0.6 has concentration 4 on this line.
At high concentration the real curve falls below the line, so the relationship is no longer proportional: dilute the sample.

checks.name: A = εcl: absorbance rises by the same amount for each unit of concentration (0.15)
at low concentration the real curve has the same gradient: it is linear in the working range
an unknown with absorbance 0.6 has concentration 4 on the calibration line
at concentration 4 the real curve is within about 15% of the line
at high concentration the real absorbance (about 1.4) is far below the line's 4.2: dilute the sample
